sources.note: Ran both passes: hybrid+EV fuel filter (37 used matches) and an efficient-gas pass filtered to Corolla/Civic/Fit/Mazda3/Elantra/Forte/Yaris (26 matches). Detail pages sit behind a Cloudflare interstitial that clears after ~10s.
106 hybrid/EV under $10k within 100mi (5 pages) plus 96 gas cars at >=32 mpg and <=115k mi sorted by deal score. Richest source for deal ratings, VINs, accident history and days-on-market.

Two OR-queries: hybrid/prius/leaf/volt/niro/ioniq/insight/ct200h (46 relevant of 200) and corolla/civic/mazda3/elantra/fit/yaris/sentra/versa/forte/cruze (29 relevant of 127). Most sub-$10k private hybrids here are 180k+ miles.

Logged in and searched 9 queries. Marketplace search is degraded today: 'hybrid' returned 14, corolla 9, elantra 8, camry hybrid 2, prius 2, nissan leaf 1, but 'honda civic', 'nissan sentra' and 'kia niro' returned 'No listings found' even after a reload + rescroll. Opened the 4 plausible cars: 186k mi, 183k mi, a rebuilt title and a 24-week-old overpriced Corolla. Nothing cleared the bar.
No inventory under $10,000. Their own price slider starts at $6,000 but the cheapest live listing sorted ascending was ~$14,000, and their quick-filter chips start at 'Under $20k'.

60 Buy-It-Now used hybrids under $10k returned, but the 100mi radius filter was not honored - 55 of 60 showed only 'Located in United States' and zero were identifiable as Colorado. Nothing verifiable within range.
Local and working. Ran prius and corolla queries (13 and 15 results). Good private-party Prius supply in Denver/Aurora; the Corolla results were mostly 145k+ mi or obvious $50/$95 scam posts.
Nothing within 100mi. Their cheapest tier page is 'under $15K' and the nearest units to 80015 were Oklahoma City (487mi), Phoenix (578mi) and Norwalk CA (834mi).
Searched Denver/Thornton with a $10k cap. They do have local inventory (Thornton, 0 mi away) but the cheapest of 21 units was $16,698 - nothing under $10k this run.
Searched Toyota Prius under $10k; 16 results but the cheapest cluster is American Fork, UT - roughly 500 miles from Aurora, five times the 100mi radius. Not worth stretching for given local supply.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan - rear bench easily swallows a rear-facing seat behind the passenger, and the LATCH anchors sit in an easy-to-reach gap.
listings.nextAction: Best all-round value on the board. Ask the dealer for the free Carfax and, given 19 open campaigns for this model year, a printout of recall work already performed.
listings.why: Great Deal, clean accident history, only 7 days listed and 5 miles from home. Midsize comfort with 41 mpg combined - the strongest blend of safety, running cost and price this run.

listings.carSeatNotes: Tall hatchback with a high roof - the easiest car here to lower a child into, and the hatch takes a stroller plus daycare bags without folding seats.
listings.nextAction: Sitting 60 days, so there is room to negotiate. Pull the accident report first and check panel gaps and paint match on the repaired corner.
listings.why: Lowest miles of any sub-$8.5k hybrid found (85k), Great Deal rating, 40 mpg, and the tall-hatch body is the most practical shape here for a car seat and daycare runs.

listings.carSeatNotes: Roomiest back seat of the whole shortlist - a rear-facing seat fits behind the driver with the front seat still comfortable for a tall adult.
listings.nextAction: Confirm the remaining hybrid-battery warranty by VIN with a Hyundai dealer; these carry a long powertrain/battery term that may still transfer.
listings.why: 5-star NHTSA overall, 40 mpg, Great Deal, and the largest rear seat here. Hyundai's hybrid battery warranty is the best in this price bracket.

listings.carSeatNotes: Hatchback with a flat floor and wide rear door opening; rear-facing fits, though check front-passenger legroom once it is installed.
listings.nextAction: Ask for a LeafSpy battery report (bars and SOH percent) before driving out - that single number decides whether this is a bargain or a headache.
listings.why: Cheapest genuinely usable car here. 2017 is the 30 kWh Lizard battery to prefer, and 63k miles is low. A 25-mile round trip is a fraction of even a degraded pack, and Level 1 charging refills that overnight.

listings.carSeatNotes: Same hatchback shape as the 2017; SL trim adds heated rear seats, a real perk for a kid in a Colorado winter.
listings.nextAction: Worth the drive to Boulder for 38k miles. Request a LeafSpy reading and confirm it is the 30 kWh pack (the VIN BZ0 code says it is).
listings.why: Only 37,994 miles - by far the lowest-mileage car under $8k found anywhere this run, with the larger 30 kWh battery, no accidents and heated rear seats.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact - this is the one to physically test with the car seat before buying; rear-facing will likely push the front passenger seat well forward.
listings.nextAction: Bring the actual car seat to the test drive. If it installs without cramping the front passenger, this is the cheapest 50 mpg on the list.
listings.why: 50 mpg combined at under $6k with Toyota hybrid reliability and only 3 days on market. The catch is size - verify car-seat fit before committing.

listings.carSeatNotes: Boxy and tall with near-vertical doors - genuinely the easiest car here to buckle a child into without stooping, and a deep cargo well behind.
listings.nextAction: Ask about battery state of health and whether the liquid-cooled pack has any service history; Soul EV packs age better than early Leafs.
listings.why: 36,755 miles and only 10 miles away. The Soul EV tall boxy cabin is the most car-seat-friendly shape on this list, and its thermally managed battery holds up better in Colorado temperature swings than an early Leaf.

listings.carSeatNotes: Full liftback with a long rear bench - more rear legroom than the Prius c and a huge hatch opening for the stroller.
listings.nextAction: Listed 2 days ago and priced as a Great Deal, so move quickly. Ask when the hybrid battery was last tested and whether the inverter coolant pump was replaced.
listings.why: 5-star safety, 48 mpg, zero accidents, and freshly listed at a Great Deal price. Mileage is high but the Gen-3 Prius routinely runs past 250k.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan, wide rear bench, good LATCH access - but the plug-in battery eats trunk space, so check the stroller fits.
listings.nextAction: Ask to see it charge on a standard outlet and confirm the plug-in battery still holds close to 19 miles of EV range.
listings.why: Plug-in with about 19 miles of electric range covers most of the daycare loop on Level 1 charging alone, then runs as a 38 mpg hybrid. Great Deal, 5-star safety, no accidents, 5 miles away.

listings.carSeatNotes: Tall hatchback like the C-Max Hybrid, so easy child loading; the plug-in battery raises the cargo floor noticeably.
listings.nextAction: 51k miles is exceptional for the price but it is a 108-mile round trip. Confirm availability and EV range by phone before driving to the Springs.
listings.why: Only 51,856 miles - the lowest-mileage plug-in found. Zero accidents and freshly listed. The distance is the tradeoff.

listings.carSeatNotes: Only four seats and a raised centre console running through the back - fine for one child seat, but it rules out a second passenger in the middle.
listings.nextAction: Confirm the roughly 38-mile EV range still holds. Only 1 open recall, which is unusually clean.
listings.why: 38 miles of EV range covers the entire commute plus daycare on electricity alone, with a gas engine as backup for winter. 5-star safety, no accidents, 5 miles away.

listings.carSeatNotes: Big midsize rear bench with excellent LATCH access - one of the two easiest cars here for a rear-facing seat.
listings.nextAction: 110 days on the lot at the top of budget means real negotiating room. Open with an offer near $9,000.
listings.why: The safest, most durable pick on the list: 5-star NHTSA, only 2 open recalls, zero accidents, Toyota hybrid drivetrain, and 4 miles from home. Priced at the ceiling but it has been sitting for 110 days.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan with a generous rear bench; plug-in battery reduces trunk depth so measure for the stroller.
listings.nextAction: Check whether the Kia 10-year hybrid-component warranty still applies by VIN - that would materially change the risk on 127k miles.
listings.why: Newest car on the list at 2018, 5-star safety, about 29 miles EV range, Good Deal, no accidents. Mileage is high but the long Kia hybrid warranty may still cover the expensive parts.

listings.carSeatNotes: Standard Leaf hatchback layout - flat floor, wide door opening, easy LATCH access.
listings.nextAction: 21,764 miles is remarkable, but this VIN is the 24 kWh pack. Get a LeafSpy report before making the 132-mile round trip to Loveland.
listings.why: Lowest mileage of anything found this run at any price. The 24 kWh pack means real winter range is roughly 50-60 miles - still ample for a 25-mile commute on Level 1 charging, but it is the reason to verify battery health first.

listings.carSeatNotes: Crossover height with a proper hatch - very easy child loading and the most cargo room of any hybrid here.
listings.nextAction: Ask for maintenance records covering the last 50k miles and check Kia hybrid-warranty eligibility by VIN.
listings.why: 49 mpg combined in a crossover body at $7,398. Zero accidents and a Good Deal rating. The 157k miles is the obvious caveat - worth it only if the service history is clean.

listings.carSeatNotes: Punches far above its size - the Fit packaging gives it rear legroom closer to a midsize, and the Magic Seat folds flat for bulky daycare gear.
listings.nextAction: Listing has no photos. Ask the dealer to text pictures and confirm condition before driving out.
listings.why: Best pure-gas pick: 34 mpg combined, 5-star NHTSA, no accidents, Great Deal, and famously cheap to run. The Fit interior space is the reason it beats every other subcompact here for a child seat.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan rear seat is adequate rather than generous - test the rear-facing install against the front passenger position.
listings.nextAction: Request the Carfax and ask whether the front passenger airbag inflator recall has been completed on this VIN.
listings.why: 33 mpg combined, 5-star NHTSA, 91k miles, 7 miles from home, and the i Touring trim adds a backup camera and blind-spot monitoring - real safety kit at this price.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact sedan - the tightest rear seat of the gas picks. Bring the car seat to try before buying.
listings.nextAction: Pull the accident report to see severity, and note this is a Mazda2 underneath, so Mazda parts and service apply.
listings.why: 36 mpg combined - the highest of any pure-gas car found - with Mazda engineering, Toyota-network servicing, and standard low-speed automatic emergency braking, which is rare at this price.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan with a surprisingly long rear bench - Sentras of this era have class-leading rear legroom.
listings.nextAction: Listed 3 days ago at a Great Deal price, so act fast. Have the CVT inspected on the test drive - that is this car's known weak point.
listings.why: Only 58,241 miles at $8,499 with zero accidents and a Great Deal rating - the best miles-per-dollar of any gas car found. Just clears the 32 mpg floor.

listings.carSeatNotes: Tall hatch, easy child loading, roomy rear bench - the same practical shape as the rank-2 C-Max.
listings.nextAction: Two accidents on record. Get the full Carfax and pay for a pre-purchase inspection focused on frame and alignment before considering it.
listings.why: Cheap 40 mpg in the most practical body style here, but two reported accidents drop it well below the rank-2 C-Max. Only worth pursuing if the inspection comes back clean.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact sedan but with unusually tall rear headroom; the trunk is large for the class, which helps with the stroller.
listings.nextAction: Have the CVT checked and confirm the service history before buying.
listings.why: 34 mpg combined, no accidents, only 2 open recalls and under $7,300. Cheap to buy and cheap to run, though it is the most basic car on the list.

listings.carSeatNotes: Long rear bench with easy LATCH access; the 2019 SV includes automatic emergency braking as standard.
listings.nextAction: Closest car on the list at 5 miles - easy to go look at. Ask for the CVT service history.
listings.why: Newest gas car found, standard automatic emergency braking, zero accidents, Good Deal, and it is right in Aurora. Exactly meets the 32 mpg floor.

listings.carSeatNotes: Roomy rear seat for a compact, with wide-opening rear doors that make a rear-facing install straightforward.
listings.nextAction: Seven open campaigns for this model year - ask the dealer to confirm which have been completed before purchase.
listings.why: The only all-wheel-drive car that clears the 32 mpg floor, with 5-star NHTSA, no accidents and a Great Deal rating. Worth considering for Colorado winters despite being the thirstiest of the gas picks.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact - same caveat as the other Prius c. Test the seat install before agreeing a price.
listings.nextAction: Private seller: ask for the VIN and a photo of the title before driving out, and meet somewhere public.
listings.why: 50 mpg and right here in Aurora at 3 miles. Longest-standing listing on the board (first seen 16 July), which suggests the seller may negotiate.

listings.carSeatNotes: Full-size Prius liftback - long rear bench and a huge hatch, much more usable than the Prius c for daycare runs.
listings.nextAction: Ask this private seller for the VIN, a photo of the title, and the recent inspection report they mention in the listing.
listings.why: Only private-party hybrid in the Denver Craigslist pool under 175k miles, posted yesterday with a recent inspection. Cheapest full-size Prius found.
